question.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of a Product Given the Necessary Data
question.problem:
For the function $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, you're given the following data:

$$
f(e)=1,\,{f}^{′}(e)=\frac{1}{e},\,g(e)={e}^{2},\,{g}^{′}(e)=2e
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=e.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x)) & =f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).\end{aligned}
$$

At the point where $x=e$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=e} & =f(e){g}^{′}(e)+g(e){f}^{′}(e) \\  & =1\cdot 2e+{e}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{e} \\  & =3e.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of a Quotient Given the Necessary Data
question.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(0)=2,\,{f}^{′}(0)=2,\,g(0)=1,\,{g}^{′}(0)=2
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=0.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=0$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=0} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(0)g(0)-f(0){g}^{′}(0)}{{g}^{2}(0)} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 1-2\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=3.$

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=3$, this gives

question.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of a Linear Combination of Functions Given the Necessary Data
question.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=-6$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-6$ | $-2\pi $ | $3\pi $ | $5$ | $-2$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)+2g(x))$ at $x=-6.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)+2g(x))={f}^{′}(x)+2{g}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=-6$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)+2g(x))|}_{x=-6} & ={f}^{′}(-6)+2{g}^{′}(-6) \\  & =5+2(-2) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of the Product or Quotient of a Composition of Functions Given the Necessary Data
question.problem:
For the functions $p(x)$ and $q(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
p(10)=-1,\,{p}^{′}(10)=-2,\,q(10)=2,\,{q}^{′}(10)=1
$$

If $z(x)=(2p(x)+q(x))(2-p(x))$, compute ${z}^{′}(10).$
question.worked_solution:
The product rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(uv)=u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=2p(x)+q(x)$ and $v=2-p(x).$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2{p}^{′}(x)+{q}^{′}(x)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=-{p}^{′}(x).
$$

Substituting this into the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}(x) & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =(2p(x)+q(x))(-{p}^{′}(x))+(2-p(x))(2{p}^{′}(x)+{q}^{′}(x)) \\  & =-{p}^{′}(x)(2p(x)+q(x))+(2{p}^{′}(x)+{q}^{′}(x))(2-p(x)).\end{aligned}
$$

At $x=10,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}(10) & =-{p}^{′}(10)(2p(10)+q(10))+(2{p}^{′}(10)+{q}^{′}(10))(2-p(10)) \\  & =-(-2)(2(-1)+2)+(2(-2)+1)(2-(-1)) \\  & =2(-2+2)-3(2+1) \\  & =0-9 \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$
